text:
maya: FYI customer ACME hitting intermittent 401s on Dedicated (GCP) after NLB -> Envoy L7 chain. They say it happens during bursts. Repro reproducible in ~1/20 requests.

sam: Can you paste a client curl and a failing response header/body? Also which model/route?

maya: Route is /v1/generate -> dedicated pool id ded-12. Sample curl:

curl -v -H "X-RW-APIKEY: ak_live_..." -H "X-RW-Timestamp: 2026-03-12T15:02:03Z" -H "X-RW-Signature: abcdef" https://dedicated-acme.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'

(today's signature obviously redacted)

jordan: attaching trimmed failing response: status 401, body {"error":"unauthorized","code":"missing_auth"}

liam: do we have envoy logs for that request? Any 502/503 upstream or header conformity warnings?

maya: yes, envoy logs show 
"request: x-rw-apikey: <REDACTED>" for success, but in many 401s the header is absent in the log when forwarded to our runtime (envoy->upstream). NLB logs show client->NLB ok.

ops-bot: @sam assigned incident RED-4532, priority P2

sam: hypothesis: NLB/forwarding chain might be normalizing or dropping custom headers during connection reuse or HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 mapping. Also check for underscore->dash drop. Our API uses underscores in X_RW_Signature? ACME used X_RW_Signature and NLB may drop headers with underscores.

maya: ACME confirms their client sends X_RW_Signature (underscore). But our internal examples use dashes (X-RW-Signature). Could be the issue.

jordan: quick test: client sent header with underscore -> reproduce locally by crafting header with underscore over HTTP/2.

jordan: repro steps I ran:
1) aws s3 proxy -> tcp dump on envoy
2) curl htps with header "X_RW_Test: 1" using http2
3) observe missing header on upstream

trace snippet:
"client -> envoy: :method: POST\n:scheme: https\n:authority: dedicated-acme...\nX_RW_Test: 1"
"envoy -> upstream: :method: POST\n:scheme: https\n:authority: runtime.internal\n"

sam: that matches known proxies that drop underscore headers per RFC. NLB/Nginx/Envoy default configs often map underscores to removed headers. Newer envoys have config option: 'allow_headers_with_underscores' or 'preserve_external_request_headers' ?

liam: there's an Envoy filter we used for header XYZ in other cases: add request_headers_to_add with exact header name, or use preserve_case and use text format. But easier: canonicalize at client -> dash.

maya: customer uses 3rd party SDK that's hard to change. We should consider a temporary fix: edge rewrite rule at our dedicated ingress to map X_RW_* -> X-RW-* before envoy forwards.

jordan: on Dedicated private we own the ingress: NLB->envoy(edge)->envoy(inner)->runtime. I can drop an Envoy lua filter to clone headers: if header with underscore exists, set equivalent dash header.

sam: do it as temporary mitigation. Also add a config in Deployments: ingress-lua-underscores-map, and alert if mapping rate > 0.1%.

liam: consequences: double-signed headers? Our HMAC verification verifies X-RW-Signature against payload and timestamp. If we duplicate header name (underscore vs dash) we must ensure runtime picks the dash header only. Update runtime to prefer X-RW-Signature (dash) and ignore underscore variant.

maya: agreed. Jordan, can you propose lua snippet?

jordan: snippet I used:

function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local h = request_handle:headers()
  local v = h:get("x_rw_signature")
  if v then h:add("x-rw-signature", v) end
  local t = h:get("x_rw_timestamp")
  if t then h:add("x-rw-timestamp", t) end
end

I put it behind a match for routes starting with /v1/

maya: deployed to canary on ded-12 ingress, monitoring now. Customer asked for ETA.

sam: ETA: 30m for canary, if stable roll in 2h. Postmortem action items: client education (dash vs underscore), runtime prefer dash, ingress mapping rule, add test in e2e for header styles.

customer-liaison: ACME notified, will test and report back. Thanks team :pray: 

maya: update 18m later: canary shows zero 401s in 600 requests. Rolling to primary now.

ops-bot: change deployed to primary for ded-12 at 2026-03-12T15:40:12Z

sam: closing with root cause: header names with underscores are dropped by proxies in chain; we added ingress mapping + runtime guard. Follow-ups: docs + SDK patch recommendation.

maya: closing thread, will open postmortem doc and link.
